subject: Mixture of gamma distributions from interval data

messages.author: a22e8a7b2a35fc51
messages.subject: Mixture of gamma distributions from interval data
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to estimate the parameters of two Gamma distributions from data assumed to come from a mixture of them.

I took the mixture of two Normal distributions example from the Stan reference and modified to use Gamma distributions and to account for my observations being an interval rather than a point, that is each x value is observed to lie between x_lower and x_upper.

data {
  int<lower=1> K; // number of mixture components
  int<lower=1> N; // number of data points
  real x_lower[N]; // interval observations: lower
  real x_upper[N]; //                        & upper
}
parameters {
  simplex[K] theta; // mixing proportions
  real<lower=0> dist_shape[K]; // shape |- of each gamma dist
  real<lower=0> dist_rate[K];  // rate  |
}
model {
  dist_shape ~ cauchy(0, 10);
  dist_rate ~ cauchy(0, 1);
  for (n in 1:N) {
    real ps[K]; // temp for log component densities
    real pp;
    for (k in 1:K) {
      pp = gamma_cdf( x_upper[n], dist_shape[k], dist_rate[k] ) -
            gamma_cdf( x_lower[n], dist_shape[k], dist_rate[k] );
      ps[k] = log(theta[k]) + log(pp);
    }
    target += log_sum_exp(ps);
  }
}

Now I'm a bit stuck. The code runs but it is very slow and doesn't mix well (high autocorrelations, traceplots look awful, big differences across chains).

I've tried it with the actual data we want to analyse and some simulated data that should be clearer (as well as having known outputs), but it doesn't appear to be working.

Any ideas how I might speed this up and improve its behaviour? Or is it just a difficult analysis to do?

Thanks.

Ron.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Mixture of gamma distributions from interval data
parts:
Do you get lots of warning messages about divergences?
If you're not seeing output in RStan, try running in one
chain. I don't know about the other interfaces but
CmdStan just pipes out warnings directly, whereas RStan
buffers them.

You might want to put tighter priors with less heavy tails
on dist_shape and dist_rate. The CDFs get very flat in the
tails.

For speed, you should compute

vector[K] log_theta = log(theta);

and reuse it rather than repeating the computation N times.

I'd normally suggest working on a log scale, but I don't know
if that'll help here given our poor log cdf implementations.

real pp = log_diff_exp(gamma_lcdf(...), gamma_lcdf(...));

At the very least, it should avoid the possible catastrophic
cancellations you get with the direct difference.

The other way you can code this model is with the latent x.
But for that, each x needs a different lower and upper bound,
which means writing your own Jacobians until we can generalize
the lower and upper bound syntax in Stan (on our to-do list).

- Bob
